suspect_claims.claim: Famileo €15.3M revenue in 2025, "growing ~9%/yr" (bottom line, Q2, comparables, largest-journal-revenue statement) [sourced-secondary: S25; estimated 15.3 ÷ 14.0]
suspect_claims.problem: The headline journal revenue was never read at source: all three Ouest-France URLs return HTTP 403, and two searches for the figure found nothing. The URL slug supports only the €16.5M 2026 target. The +9% divides an unread snippet by a rounded "près de 14 millions". A source the file already cites (S20, JDD, 2025-02-20) has the founder saying "un chiffre d'affaires d'à peu près 15 millions d'euros", which the file omits; on that base growth is nearer 2% than 9%. S18 also shows 2025 was forecast at €16M, so €15.3M would be a miss. The largest directly read figure is "près de 14 millions" (2024, S18).

suspect_claims.claim: Aura "≥$56M/yr at retail value" and "implied connected frames ≈ 2.5M" (Q1, comparables table revenue cell)
suspect_claims.problem: Presented as a floor (≥) but the method cannot give one. 10M "people" ÷ 4 contributors per frame is not a lower bound on cumulative frames sold, since people overlap across frames and owners are counted. Multiplying by the $149 list price ignores wholesale to Amazon/Best Buy and discounting (the site shows $139 today). It is the only Aura revenue-like number in the comparables table. Arithmetic reproduces (375k × $149 = $55.9M); the premise does not.

suspect_claims.claim: Skylight: "now claims '$300M+' ... most of it from a kitchen calendar, not the grandparent frame" and "the nine-figure outcome (Skylight) came from moving off the grandparent frame"
suspect_claims.problem: The $300M+ quote is real (Wellfound: "scaled this business to $300M+ in annual revenue while being completely bootstrapped and profitable") but the listing is undated. The file's own S10 (2026-07-31, president quoted) says "more than $500 million in annual revenue"; the two company claims differ by 67% and are not reconciled, and the largest-revenue statement leads with the lower, undated one. The calendar-led mix is asserted as fact while the file marks Frame-vs-Calendar split [unknown]; Skylight was already $30M in 2019 and $75M in 2021 on a calendar launched in 2020. Forbes Brasil (S8) also says 2022 sales were planned flat and the user base was 5 million; both omitted. All Skylight revenue is unaudited company claim or press.

suspect_claims.claim: Chatbooks churn: "49,000 active subscriptions churned" (2024); "150K subscriptions canceled in 2025"; cancellation rate "86% of sub orders" → 66% [sourced-secondary: S30]
suspect_claims.problem: Quotes match the page, but the whole Chatbooks churn case is one designer's self-published portfolio. The 86%/66% is the share of subscription orders entering the cancel flow that completed cancellation ("across 69,000+ sub orders in the measurement period"), not a subscriber churn rate; the numbers table lists it as "86% → 66%" with no denominator. 49,000 (2024) against 150K (2025) is a threefold jump the file does not question. Q7 leans on "Chatbooks cancelled 150K subscriptions in 2025" as falsification evidence without any subscriber base to compare against.

suspect_claims.claim: "The US shows no journal traction" / Famileo US "traction is negligible" (110 US iOS ratings vs 5,322 France); "No US senior-living operator announcing Famileo was found [unknown]"
suspect_claims.problem: Rating counts verified (110 / 5,321 today), but storefront rating count is an unvalidated proxy stated as a finding; Famileo itself claims "4,8/5 from 42,000 reviews on App Store and Google Play". The senior-living statement is contradicted by the file's own S23: the Famileo Pro US page carries testimonials from Welch Senior Living ("Duxbury House at the Village") and "The Lakes of Monclova". Hug Letters' page shows a TODAY Show Deals placement, also unreported. US traction is thin but not evidenced as zero.

suspect_claims.claim: Unit-economics scenario: "print $2.50 [assumption] ... COGS $5.37, gross margin 46% at $9.99"
suspect_claims.problem: The only gross-margin figure in the file rests on a print cost with no source, quote or method. Postage uses retail single-piece flats ($2.27) although the cited Notice 123 also publishes commercial, Marketing Mail and Periodicals flats prices that the file says it did not read. The 46% is arithmetic on an invented input.

suspect_claims.claim: Nixplay FY2022/FY2023 figures: revenue $30,487,490 / $20,038,285, net loss $7,557,913 / $5,023,536, Plus "approximately 10,000" (+31%), 3.5M users → ~42,300 subs, ~1.2% paying [sourced: S14]
